images.caption: Figure 1:GameRealm overview. GameRealm spans diverse games and supports multiple tasks: single-view, multi-view, and panoramic world modeling, alongside stereo, multi-view reconstruction, and point tracking. The collage showcases original game ground-truth data totaling over 120 million frames and 1,000 hours.
Figure 2:Data acquisition pipeline

Figure 3:Data collection. GameRealm encompasses diverse game environments, first- and third-person perspectives, and a wide range of playable characters, including humans and animals. Data are acquired through two complementary strategies: human-driven collection for interaction-rich scenarios (top) and automated collection for free-roaming scenarios (bottom)

Figure 4:Examples of retained video clips after quality filtering.
The selected clips maintain clear scene visibility and coherent temporal progression across diverse game environments, providing reliable visual observations for downstream spatial understanding tasks.

Figure 5:Examples of rejected video clips during quality filtering.
Clips with severe underexposure or overexposure, abnormal in-game visual effects (e.g., poisoning), or substantial view occlusions are excluded due to degraded scene visibility and visual reliability.

Figure 8:Scene. The first row shows human-oriented environments, including indoor spaces, urban streets, and outer space, while the second row presents natural environments such as snowfields, forests, lava fields, and lakes.

Figure 9:Weather. The first row illustrates weather conditions, including rain, snow, and fog, while the second row shows the progression of time from pre-dawn and morning through noon, dusk, and late night.
Figure 10:Character. Representative examples of character diversity in GameRealm, including robots, fish, birds, dragons, humans, and many others.
Figure 11:Interaction. Representative interaction activities in GameRealm, including motorcycle riding, driving, skiing, opening doors, jumping, and other diverse gameplay interactions.

Figure 26:Reconstruction Comparison. Qualitative reconstruction comparisons on motorcycle-riding (top) and snow-sports (bottom) sequences. From left to right: sampled input frames, the originalπ3\pi^{3}, baseline fine-tuning, and fine-tuning with GameRealm (ours). Compared with the reference models, our method produces more spatially distributed reconstructions, with successive subject observations more clearly separated along the visible path.

Figure 27:3D tracking during character interaction. Top to bottom: ground truth, TAPIP3D, and TAPIP3D∗fine-tuned on our game data. Matching colors identify the same query points across rows and frames.
